newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wrightson falls after forecast lowered.
newsitem.headline: Wrightson falls after forecast lowered.

text.p: Shares in New Zealand rural servicing company Wrightson Ltd fell sharply after the company reported a much reduced first half profit and predicted a hefty reduction in its full year profit.
Wrightson shares fell nine cents to 95 NZ cents 45 minutes after the announcement at noon (2300 GMT).
The company announced a half year profit of NZ$1.25 milliion against the previous $5.74 million, and cut its full year forecast to $12-16 million from an adjusted previous forecast of $20-23 million.
Company executives told a briefing that its profit had been affected by adverse trading conditions which they expect to continue for some time.
A lower first half dividend of 2.5 cents from 3.5 cents also contributed to the gloom.
Despite the profit fall, most analysts said most of the negative news had been well telegraphed by the company.
One, who declined to be identified, said the new profit forecast was not too far off the previous one if "normalised" for one-offs and foregone earnings from divested assets.
He had expected the lower dividend, and the first half earnings were in the forecast range.
He said Wrightson was a good prospect for investors looking for a recovery stock.
O'Connor agreed with Wrightson Chief Executive Greg Kay that the outlook was for an improvement in commodity prices to help restore earnings.
"It looks like we are at the bottom of the trough. The question is whether we wallow at the bottom of the trough for a long time or if we are actually about to bounce," he said.
"I do think earnings will go up but it is not going to be easy," he said.
